question_text: A 17-year-old male is brought to the emergency department following a motor vehicle accident. He has suffered several wounds and is minimally responsive. There is a large laceration on his forehead as well as a fracture of his nasal bridge. He appears to be coughing and spitting blood. He is already wearing a soft collar. Vitals are as follows: T 36.4C, BP 102/70 mmHg, HR 126 bpm, and RR 18 rpm, and SpO2 is 88% on RA. He has 2 peripheral IVs and received 2L of IV normal saline on route to the hospital. There is frank blood in the oropharynx. Breath sounds are present bilaterally. Abdomen is distended and tender. Pulses are 1+. Which of the following should be the first step in management?
